title: ESA VALIDATION DATA CENTRE (EVDC) NOVA - EVOLUTION AND OPERATIONS - EXPRO+
description: The ESA atmospheric Validation Data Center (EVDC) provides centralized access to correlative Cal/Val data sets, such as Fiducial Reference Measurements (FRM), sondes, aircraft, and balloon campaigns. These are used to validate satellite-based atmospheric composition products. Since 2016, the EVDC has undergone significant modernization and evolution, introducing advanced functionalities and tools for the Cal/Val community, including an Orbit Prediction and Overpass Tool, access to satellite data (e.g., Sentinel-5P, EarthCARE), DOI self-assignment for ground-based datasets, and dedicated support for the EarthCARE user community. This tender addresses the next phase of the EVDC's evolution: EVDC Nova. This initiative will establish the foundations for a robust, operational multi-mission platform while ensuring the complete continuity of existing services

title: MINIATURIZATION OF NITROGEN-VACANCY CENTER-BASED MAGNETOMETERS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:  To develop a space proven NV-Centred Diamond magnetometer with reduced SWaP. Description:  Magnetic field measurements from low Earth orbit are important for understanding Earth's magnetosphere, monitoring of space weather, and studying geophysical processes. These measurements provide insights into solar-terrestrial interactions and help mitigate risks to both orbital infrastructure and terrestrial systems. NV -centres magnetometers are recent developments that have been successfully implemented on the ISS. Next to their scientific interest, one of their applications lays in using the magnetic field for AOCS purposes in space. Using a magnetic map, the full attitude of the spacecraft can be followed. This has been demonstrated during the first Ariane launch where one of these systems could follow the first minutes of the trajectory of the rocket. There is now the need to further develop such system to allow them to be utilized for navigation of spacecrafts or on other bodies (which have a magnetic field) with a specific focus on reduction of size and mass of the instrument to be integrated to AOCS system. The development shall be focused on miniaturisation and reduction of resources and on increasing the resolution of the magnetometers to pT.  This activity encompasses the following tasks:  - Consolidation of technical requirements given application in miniature quantum devices and preliminary design.- Detailed design of the magnetometer. - Manufacturing, integration and functional verification. - Test campaign, outcomes and development plan to qualification. Deliverables: Breadboard, Reports

title: COMPACT LASER SYSTEMS FOR ALKALI RYDBERG ATOMIC SENSORS - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a low SwaP breadboard of a full laser system that will manipulate Rydberg atom in vapour cell, and be able tobe configured for sensing applications for RF receivers.Description: Highly-excited atoms, often known as Rydberg atoms, display extreme sensitivity to external electromagnetic (EM) fields, including the electric fields associated with black-body radiation (BBR).In addition to their use in quantum computing, Rydberg atoms can be configured for sensing applications. Such sensors make use of non-destructive read-out of Rydberg states, which is implemented optically, including fluorescence detection of low-lying Rydberg states. A range of different Rydberg sensing modalities have been developed; these include those developed for microwave standards andimaging in the Terahertz regime to sensitive digital communications techniques in radio and microwave bands. This activity developsa complete laser system needed to perform an RF instrument based on Alkali Rydberg Atomic Sensors. To do so the selection of the relevant parameters to address the sensor is aimed to be done by consolidating the first set of requirements. A dedicated focus is to be addressed towards a low SWaP (Size, Weight and Power) for CubeSAT platform. This shall ensure a proper design and manufacturing of the Laser system. This breadboard is then tested on an adequate Rydberg sensor for RF measurement. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirement review for laser system to manipulate Rydberg atom - Design of a compact laser system - Manufacturing of the laser system - Test on Rydberg Atom and validation of the RF instrument.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators. title: AI ASSISTED SYSML V2 SPACE MODEL INTERACTION AND KNOWLEDGE REUSE - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop and validate an AI-based assistant for interactive access, querying and assisted manipulation of SysML v2 space system models to reduce modelling effort and increase design quality.Description:Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) is an approach to manage the complexity of future space systems.Working effectively with large digital models is challenging; understanding structure and dependencies,reusing assets across projects, and extracting decision-relevant information is time-consuming andexpert-dependent.Limited and non-intuitive access to very large models slows MBSE adoption and reduces the return oninvestments, especially in early phases where it drives duplication, and late inconsistency discovery causeshigher design risk. SysML v2 introduces combined textual and graphical modelling with a standardised API for programmatic access, which lowers the access barrier. AI - and particularly Large Language Models (LLMs) - can help translate user intent into controlled, explainable interactions with these formal SysML v2 models, overcoming the barriers identified.This activity will develop an AI assistant that acts as an intermediate layer between users and formal modelsand operates exclusively via the SysML v2 textual notation and standard API. It will support (i) natural-language assistance for incremental model creation and modification, (ii) model querying and automated consistency checking, (iii) guided exploration of dependencies, (iv) identification and extraction of reusable model elements, and (v) structured summarization of model content for expert and non-expert stakeholders. The focus is on human assistance, incremental model generation and knowledge exploitation that helps system engineerswork with large system models - not on autonomous end-to-end model generation or mission-specifictoolchains.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of SysML v2 capabilities, APIs, and relevant AI techniques for model creation and interaction- Identification of representative use cases for querying, exploration, and reuse of SysML v2 models- Definition of a reference architecture ensuring controlled AI interaction via the SysML v2 API- Development of proof-of-concept AI components for model generation, querying and summarization- Validation of the approach on representative SysML v2 models, using the ESA MBSE methodology- Assessment of benefits, limitations, and roadmap towards higher TRL.The activity will result in validated concepts, software prototypes, and documented lessons learned, enablingfollow-on developments under GSTP or other programmes focusing on operational deployment.Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entitieswithin ESA Member States can access it and can provide update to the community of users.
